newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian budget to focus on 98/99 - Costello.
newsitem.headline: Australian budget to focus on 98/99 - Costello.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Sunday that the hard work in reducing the budget deficit had been done last year, and the focus on this year's budget would be on restoring balance by the 1998/99 year to June 30.

The budget, which Costello will deliver on May 13, will not contain the same dimension of cuts as the 1996/97 one, and areas where big structural changes were made in the 1996/97 budget, such as higher education and aged care, will not be returned to, Costello said in an interview on the Seven network.
"The important thing we're focusing on is not so much this coming year 1997/98, but 1998/99," Costello said.
The Budget mid-year review, released in January, projected a deficit of A$2.2 billion on a no-policy change basis for 1998/99.
The Treasury also estimated then that the starting point for the year to June 1998 was A$3.9 billion, compared with a forecast A$8.5 billion for 1996/97.
"Because we broke the back of the work in the last budget, we didn't finish it ... that means that the task is not going to be as great this year," he said.

"It's not easy because its coming on top of savings already put in place, but it's not of the dimensions that it was in the past," C into balance over the course of the parliament, so the government was focusing on achieving that in 1998/99.
"We've made extraordinary progress there, sure we got knocked around a bit in the senate, but last year we've bought down a savings package of A$7.2 billion over two years," he said.
While achieving balance would require further fiscal tightening, it would not be to the extent announced in the last budget.
The extra savings needed to achieve balance would not be sought form areas that had been heavily affected in the 1996/97 budget, he said.
